questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution is related with the oath or affirmation by judges of high courts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**219**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Appointment of Judges of the High Courts is made under Articles 217 and 224 of the Constitution of India.
 
• Article 217 - Appointment and conditions of the office of a Judge of a High Court
 
 
• Every Judge of a High Court shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal. *Hence statement 1 is correct.*
 
• A person shall not be qualified for appointment as a Judge of a High Court unless he is a citizen of India and—
 
• has for at least ten years held a judicial office in the territory of India; or
 
• has for at least ten years been an advocate of a High Court or of two or more such Courts in succession;
 
 
 
• Article 219 - Oath or affirmation by Judges of High Courts.
 
 
• Every person appointed to be a Judge of a High Court shall, before he enters upon his office, make and subscribe before the Governor of the State, or some person appointed on that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the Third Schedule. *Hence statement 2 is correct.*
 
 
 
• Article 224 - Appointment of additional and acting Judges.
 
 
• If by reason of any temporary increase in the business of a High Court or by reason of arrears of work therein, it appears to the President that the 

 number of the Judges of that Court should be for the time being increased, duly qualified persons to be Additional Judges of the Court for such period not exceeding two years as he may specify.
 
• When any Judge of a High Court other than the Chief Justice is by reason of absence or for any another reason unable to perform the duties of his office or is appointed to act temporarily as Chief Justice,a duly qualified person to act as a Judge of that Court until the permanent Judge has resumed his duties.
 
• No person appointed as an additional or acting Judge of a High Court shall hold office after attaining the age of 62 years.
 
 
 
• Appointment of Judges of the High Courts is made under Articles 217 and 224 of the Constitution of India, which do not provide for reservation for any caste or class of persons.

questions.question:
An information is given, followed by two statements labelled I and II. Identify which of the statements is/are possible reason(s) behind the given information.

**Information:**

Due to COVID, schools will have to operate on a hybrid model i.e. online as well as physical school.

**Statements:**

I. Many parents are still not willing to send their children to places with large gatherings owing to a pandemic

II. In schools, seating capacity will not be adequate to accommodate all the enrolled students owing to the social distancing norms.

options.text: Neither statement I nor II is a possible reason.
Both statements I and II are possible reasons.
Only statement I is a possible reason.
Only statement II is a possible reason.

questions.solution:
• The existence of a pandemic and its spread due to large gatherings can discourage many parents from sending their children to school. Thus, statement I is a possible reason.
 
• Social distance norms would cause the requirement of increase in seating capacity to accommodate the original number of students. However, this might not be feasible for all schools. Thus, online or a hybrid model would be an appropriate choice in such a situation. Therefore, statement II is also a possible reason.

Hence, **"Both statements I and II are possible reasons."** is the correct answer.

questions.question: If 6y² − 13y + 6 = 0, then find the product of the two roots of the equation.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

6y² − 13y + 6 = 0

**Formula used:**

For any quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0

The product of the roots = c/a.

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

a = 6, b = -13, and c = 6

Now,

The product of the roots = c/a = 6/6 = 1

∴ The product of the two roots of the equation is 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

**Concept used:**

ax² + bx + c = 0

a, b, c = Known numbers,

Where a ≠ 0, x = Unknown

**Calculation:**

6y2 − 13y + 6 = 0

⇒ 6y2 − 9y - 4y + 6 = 0

⇒ 3y(2y − 3) - 2(2y - 3) = 0

⇒ (2y − 3)(3y - 2) = 0

⇒ y = 3/2 and 2/3

Now, According to the question,

(3/2) × (2/3) = 1

**∴ The product of the two roots of the equation is 1.**

questions.question: The surface area of a sphere is 61600 sq. cm. Find the volume of the sphere (in cu m). [Use π = (22)/(7)]

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Volume** of a sphere in terms of **Surface Area (SA)** and **radius (r)** is given by: Volume = (SA × r) ÷ 3

First, find **radius**: r² = SA ÷ 4π = 61600 ÷ (4 × 22/7) = 4900 ⇒ r = 70 cm.

Volume in cm³ = (61600 × 70) ÷ 3 = 4312000/3 cm³.

Convert to **m³** (1 m³ = 10⁶ cm³): (4312000/3) ÷ 1,000,000 = 4.312/3 m³.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.312/3 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Surface Area** of sphere = 61600 cm²

**Value of π** = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area = 4πr²

Volume = (4/3)πr³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/54b73ba1f90948818ddab0865e951bb1ed4509a507cc7d4c20b8e2c225c0078b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4 × (22/7) × r² = 61600

⇒ (88/7) × r² = 61600

⇒ r² = (61600 × 7) ÷ 88

⇒ r² = 700 × 7 = 4900

⇒ **r** = √4900 = 70 cm

⇒ Volume (V) = (4/3) × (22/7) × 70 × 70 × 70

⇒ V = (4/3) × 22 × 10 × 70 × 70

⇒ V = (88 × 49000) ÷ 3 = 4312000/3 cm³

To convert **cm³** to **m³**, divide by 10⁶ (since 1 m = 100 cm):

⇒ V = (4312000/3) ÷ 1,000,000

⇒ V = 4.312/3 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 4.312/3 m³.**

A circular racing track has been developed in a field. If the difference between the outer circumference and the inner circumference of the racing track is 33 m, then find the width of the track (in m).

(Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The difference between the outer circumference and the inner circumference of the racing track is 33 m

**Concept used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2πr

Here r = radius

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f40934c215c537dd2376a12665ceb06d708a78ca037bb9e50752a0d0022cb91b.png] 

Let the radius of the outer circle be R and the inner circle be r

Now,

2πR - 2πr = 33

⇒ 2π(R - r) = 33

⇒ (R - r) = 33 × (1/2π)

⇒ (R - r) = 33 × (7/44)

⇒ (R - r) = 21/4 = 5(1)/(4)

So, width of the track = 5(1)/(4) m

questions.question: In a mixture of 90 litres, the ratio of milk to water is 4 ∶ 1. In another mixture of 90 litres, the ratio of milk to water is 3 ∶ 2. What is the positive difference between the quantities of milk in the two mixtures?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total volume is 90 litres for both mixtures and total ratio parts are 5 for both (4 + 1 = 5 and 3 + 2 = 5).

Difference in milk ratio parts directly = 4 − 3 = 1 part.

Since 5 parts = 90 litres, 1 part = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 litres.

Thus, the difference in the quantity of milk is 18 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Mixture 1 (90L)
 
 
 
 Water: 1 part
 
 
 
 Milk: 4 parts (72L)

 
 Mixture 2 (90L)
 
 
 
 Water: 2 parts
 
 
 
 Milk: 3 parts (54L)

 
 
• 
 Milk Difference = 72L - 54L = 18L

**Given:**

Total quantity of Mixture 1 = 90 litres

Ratio of milk to water in Mixture 1 = 4 : 1

Total quantity of Mixture 2 = 90 litres

Ratio of milk to water in Mixture 2 = 3 : 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total ratio parts in Mixture 1 = 4 + 1 = 5 parts

⇒ Quantity of milk in Mixture 1 = 90 × (4 ÷ 5) = 72 litres

⇒ Total ratio parts in Mixture 2 = 3 + 2 = 5 parts

⇒ Quantity of milk in Mixture 2 = 90 × (3 ÷ 5) = 54 litres

⇒ Positive difference between the quantities of milk = 72 − 54 = 18 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 18 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixing Multiple Mixtures

When combining multiple mixtures, it is easiest to find the individual fractional quantities of each component (e.g., milk and water) for each mixture before adding them together to find the final overall ratio.

It helps to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices or concentrations must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired average price or concentration.

Replacement Method

When a certain volume of mixture is repeatedly replaced by a solvent (like water), the remaining amount of the pure element after n replacements is: Final = Initial × (1 − Replacement Volume ÷ Total Volume)ⁿ.

questions.question: Sudhir is 4.5 times as efficient as Aarav. If they work together, they can complete a piece of work in 8 days. How many days will Aarav take to do the same work alone?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **efficiency** between **Sudhir** and **Aarav** = 4.5 : 1 → 9 : 2

Total efficiency of both working together = 9 + 2 = 11 units/day

**Total Work** = Total Efficiency × Time = 11 × 8 = 88 units

Time taken by **Aarav** alone = Total Work ÷ Aarav's Efficiency = 88 ÷ 2 = 44 days

**∴ The correct answer is 44 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Sudhir's efficiency** is 4.5 times that of **Aarav**.

⇒ Time taken by both to complete the work = 8 days.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Individual Time = Total Work ÷ Individual Efficiency

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Sudhir
 9.77
 88
 9
 
 

 Aarav
 44
 2
 
 

⇒ Let the **efficiency** of **Aarav** be 2 units/day.

⇒ Then, the **efficiency** of **Sudhir** = 4.5 × 2 = 9 units/day.

⇒ Combined efficiency of **Sudhir + Aarav** = 9 + 2 = 11 units/day.

⇒ **Total work** to be completed = 11 units/day × 8 days = 88 units.

⇒ Time taken by **Aarav** alone = 88 units ÷ 2 units/day = 44 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 44 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency-Time Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to time. If person A is n times more efficient than B, A will take 1/n of the time taken by B.

Combined Work Formula

If two people with efficiencies E₁ and E₂ work together for D days, the total work is (E₁ + E₂) × D.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed based on the **ratio of work done**, which is the product of efficiency and the time for which they worked.</p

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 9,800 was invested for a year at 10% interest per annum, compounded half-yearly. What would been the interest payable at the end of the year?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate becomes 5% (10% ÷ 2) and periods become 2 (1 year × 2).

Effective interest rate for 2 periods at 5% = 5 + 5 + (5 × 5)/100 = 10.25%.

Total interest = 10.25% of ₹9,800.

Calculation: 9800 × 0.1025 = 1004.5.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,004.50.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹9,800

Annual Rate (R) = 10% per annum

Time (T) = 1 year

**Formula Used:**

For **compounding half-yearly**:

New Rate (r) = R/2 | New Time (n) = T × 2

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Interest (CI) = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b3ca8abc27e8580d0844fb2128d140eec9f949c2a7db76f94808b34b60acebd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ r = 10% ÷ 2 = 5%

⇒ n = 1 × 2 = 2 half-years

⇒ A = 9800(1 + 5/100)²

⇒ A = 9800(1 + 0.05)²

⇒ A = 9800(1.05)²

⇒ A = 9800 × 1.1025

⇒ A = ₹10,804.50

⇒ CI = 10804.50 − 9800

⇒ CI = ₹1,004.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,004.50.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compounding Frequency

For half-yearly, rate is halved (R/2) and time is doubled (2T). For quarterly, rate is R/4 and time is 4T.

Effective Rate Formula

Successive percentage change formula: a + b + (ab/100) helps find net interest rate for multiple periods.

Compound vs Simple Interest

In the first period (if compounding frequency matches time), CI equals SI. From the second period, CI is always greater than SI.

{2.1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.3, 11, 15, 17, 19.21, 27, 31, 31, 33, 16.5, 14, 10}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the data in **ascending order** to find the middle term.

The **Mode** is the most frequently occurring value, which is 31.

The **Median** for 17 terms is the 9th term, which is 14.

Required **Difference** = 31 − 14 = 17.

**∴ The correct answer is 17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data set = {2.1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.3, 11, 15, 17, 19.21, 27, 31, 31, 33, 16.5, 14, 10}

**Formula Used:**

1. **Mode** = Value with the highest frequency.

2. **Median** (if n is odd) = ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term of the sorted data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a1992ca9a18d25af89690437a7f08f2e5d0116cc2d04fe349b299daaa044a332.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Arrange in ascending order: 2.1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.3, 10, 11, **14**, 15, 16.5, 17, 19.21, 27, **31**, **31**, 33

⇒ Total number of observations (n) = 17

⇒ **Median** = ((17 + 1) ÷ 2)th term = 9th term

⇒ 9th term = 14

⇒ In the data set, 31 occurs twice, which is the highest frequency.

⇒ **Mode** = 31

⇒ Required Difference = |Median − Mode|

⇒ Difference = 31 − 14 = 17

**∴ The correct answer is 17.**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Median for Even observations

If n is even, Median = Average of (n ÷ 2)th and ((n ÷ 2) + 1)th terms.

Range of Data

Range = Maximum Value − Minimum Value. For this set, Range = 33 − 2.1 = 30.9.</p

questions.question: A can complete 12% of the work in 15% of the allotted time. A and B worked for the entire period of the allotted time and the work got completed on time. What portion of the work was done by B?

12% of work is completed in 15 minutes by A

questions.question: When we divide NNP (Net national product) by the total population of a nation we get _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**per capita income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When we divide NNP by the total population of a nation we get the per capita income.
 
 
• Per Capita Income= NNP/ Total Population__*__.__*
 
 

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Net national product (NNP) is the gross national product (GNP), the total value of finished goods and services produced by a country's citizens **overseas** and domestically, minus depreciation.
 
• NNP is often examined on an annual basis as a way to measure a nation's success in continuing minimum production standards.
 
• It can be a useful method to keep track of an economy as it takes into account all its citizens, regardless of where they make their money, and acknowledges the fact that capital must be spent to keep production standards high.
 
• The NNP is expressed in the currency of the nation it represents. That means that in the United States the NNP is expressed in dollars (USD), while for the European Union (EU) member nations the NNP is expressed in euros (EUR).
 
• The NNP can be extrapolated from the **GNP** by subtracting the depreciation of any assets. The depreciation figure is determined by assessing the loss of the value of assets attributed to normal use and aging.
 
• The relationship between a nation's GNP and NNP is similar to the relationship between its gross domestic product (GDP) and net domestic product (NDP).

Average = Sum of elements/No. of elements

**Calculation:**

Total weight of 14 students = 14 × 20

⇒ 280 kg

After a student left the class total weight of the class = (20 - 2) × 13

⇒ 18 × 13 = 234 kg

questions.question: Arushi was to multiply a number by 2.4, but instead multiplied by 4.2. If the product she obtained was 65.1, then what is the correct product that she should have got?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of multipliers: **Correct** : **Incorrect** = 2.4 : 4.2 = 4 : 7.

Since the original number is the same, the products are proportional to the multipliers.

7 units (Incorrect product) = 65.1

1 unit = 65.1 ÷ 7 = 9.3

4 units (Correct product) = 4 × 9.3 = 37.20

**∴ The correct answer is 37.20.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Incorrect multiplier = 4.2, Incorrect product = 65.1, Correct multiplier = 2.4.

**Formula Used:** Correct Product = (Incorrect Product ÷ Incorrect Multiplier) × Correct Multiplier

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/343b16fa9dc2f038bb8ea93fec4d7dfb377a077e8cb6e25dbd23a0424e5dbc03.png]

⇒ x = 651 ÷ 42 = 15.5

⇒ The correct product should have been: 2.4 × x

⇒ Correct Product = 2.4 × 15.5

⇒ Correct Product = 37.20

**∴ The correct answer is 37.20.**

**__Additional Information__**

Proportionality in Multiplication

If a constant number is multiplied by different factors, the products are directly proportional to those factors: P₁/M₁ = P₂/M₂.

questions.question: The intervention by the monetary authority of a country in the money market to keep the money supply stable against external shocks is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sterilisation.**__

__
 
• **The intervention by the monetary authority of a country in the money market to keep the money supply stable against external shocks is called Sterilisation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sterilisation **refers to the process by which the RBI takes away money from the banking system to neutralise the fresh money that enters the system.
 
• Suppose the RBI decides to buy US dollars (USD) from the market. Now, the money held by the RBI does not form part of the banking system.
 
• So, if the RBI releases rupees from its coffers to buy dollars, the money supply in the banking system increases.
 
• That can be a problem.
 
• If the volume of goods and services produced in the economy remains unchanged, the extra money will lead to an increase in the prices of all commodities.
 
• More money in the banking system means higher bond prices because banks will have more money, and they will buy more bonds.
 
• And that will push up bond prices. Since bonds carry an inverse price-yield relationship, higher bond prices mean lower yields.
 
• The problem is that lower yields will force the RBI to cut interest rates further.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ratio of money held by the public in currency to that they hold in bank deposits is the Currency Deposit Ratio (CDR). 

 
 
• ​This reflects liquidity in the system. 
 
• The proportion of the** ****total deposits **commercial banks keeps as reserves are the Reserve Ratio. 
 
• **It includes:**
 
 

 
 

 
 
**Cash Reserve Ratio**

 
 
 
It is the **fraction of money** that banks must deposit with the RBI. Banks do not earn any interest on this amount. 

 
 
 

 
 
**Statutory Liquidity Ratio**

 
 
 
It is the fraction of **the total deposits of a bank** that must be kept in a **liquid form**. Banks can use this money to purchase **Government Securities (G-Sec).**

questions.question: The present average age of X, Y and Z is 44 years. 8 years ago the average age of X and Y was 38 years. What is the present age of Z?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present total age of **X, Y, and Z** = 44 × 3 = 132 years.

Present average age of **X and Y** = 38 + 8 = 46 years.

Present total age of **X and Y** = 46 × 2 = 92 years.

Present age of **Z** = 132 − 92 = 40 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present average of **X, Y, and Z** = 44 years

Average of **X and Y** (8 years ago) = 38 years

**Formula Used:**

**Sum of ages = Average age × Number of persons**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/645a43274bce51ee520f71173a8083995c7696d3296e2fd616733a46b97c6ebe.png] 

⇒ Total present age of **X, Y, and Z** = 44 × 3 = 132 years.

⇒ Total age of **X and Y** (8 years ago) = 38 × 2 = 76 years.

⇒ Present total age of **X and Y** = 76 + (8 × 2) = 76 + 16 = 92 years.

⇒ Present age of **Z** = (Total age of X, Y, Z) − (Total age of X, Y)

⇒ Age of **Z** = 132 − 92 = 40 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Age Increment

If the age of each person in a group increases by **n** years after a period of **n** years, the **average age** of the group also increases by exactly **n** years.

Sum of Observations

Age Difference Constant

The numerical **difference** between the ages of any two individuals remains **constant** throughout their lives.</p

questions.question: Evaluate frac{cos²(45circ+theta)+cos²(45circ−theta)}{{cosec}² 30circ sin² 45circ−sec² 60circ}.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **complementary angle** property where cos(45o+θ) = sin(45o−θ).

The numerator becomes **sin²(45o−θ) + cos²(45o−θ) = 1**.

Substitute standard values in the denominator: **(2)² × (1/√2)² − (2)² = 4 × (1/2) − 4 = −2**.

The final value is 1 / −2 = −1/2.

**∴ The correct answer is −1/2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cos²(45o+θ) + cos²(45o−θ) / (cosec² 30o × sin² 45o − sec² 60o)

**Formula Used:** **cos(90o − A) = sin A**; **sin² A + cos² A = 1**; **cosec 30o = 2**; **sin 45o = 1/√2**; **sec 60o = 2**.

⇒ **Numerator** = cos²(45o + θ) + cos²(45o − θ)

⇒ Let A = 45o + θ. Then 90o − A = 45o − θ.

⇒ Numerator = sin²(90o − (45o + θ)) + cos²(45o − θ)

⇒ Numerator = sin²(45o − θ) + cos²(45o − θ) = 1

⇒ **Denominator** = cosec² 30o × sin² 45o − sec² 60o

⇒ Denominator = (2)² × (1/√2)² − (2)²

⇒ Denominator = 4 × (1/2) − 4

⇒ Denominator = 2 − 4 = −2

⇒ **Final Value** = 1 / −2 = −1/2

**∴ The correct answer is −1/2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Complementary Angle Relations

For any angle θ, sin(90o−θ) = cosθ, tan(90o−θ) = cotθ, and sec(90o−θ) = cosecθ.

Standard Values Table

sin 30o = 1/2, sin 45o = 1/√2, sin 60o = √3/2; cos values are the reverse. cosec, sec, and cot are reciprocals of sin, cos, and tan.</p

questions.question: The power of the Parliament to Amend the Constitution of India is described in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 368**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Part XX of Article 368 empowers the Parliament to amend Constitution by way of addition, variation or repeal of any provision according to the procedure laid down therein, which is different from the procedure for ordinary legislation.
 
• Article 368 has been amended by the 24th and 42nd Amendments in 1971 and 1976 respectively. New clauses 368 (1) and 368 (3) were added by the 24th Amendment in 1971, which also added a new clause (4) in article 13 which reads, **"Nothing in this article shall apply to any amendment of this Constitution made under article 368."**
 
• Amending the constitution of India is the process of making amendments to the fundamental law or supreme law of the country.
 
• The amendment process in the constitution is set out in Part XX (Article 368) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This procedure preserves the sanctity of India's Constitution and holds a check on the Indian Parliament's arbitrary power.
 
• **Article 368** does not set down the legislative process to be followed at various points of the amendment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first amendment was made to the Indian Constitution in 1951.
 
• The Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, enacted in 1951, made several changes to the Fundamental Rights provisions of the Indian constitution.
 
• It provided means to restrict freedom of speech and expression, validation of zamindari abolition laws, and clarified that the right to equality does not bar the enactment of laws that provide "special consideration" for weaker sections of society.
 
• The formal title of the amendment is the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951.
 
• It was moved by the then Prime Minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, on 10 May 1951 and enacted by Parliament on 18 June 1951.

Given:

The ratio of the length, width, and height of a cuboid is 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 5 and the sum of the lengths of all its edges is 144 cm.

Concept used:

The surface area of cuboid = 2 (lw + wh + lh) square units 

where l, w, h are denoted as length, width, and height respectively.

The number of edges of a cuboid is 12. 

Calculation:

Let the common ratio be Q.

Hence, the length, width, and height of the cuboid be 4Q, 3Q, and 5Q respectively.

According to the question,

4 × (4Q + 3Q + 5Q) = 144

⇒ Q = 3

Hence, the surface area of the cuboid

⇒ 2 (4Q × 3Q + 4Q × 5Q + 3Q × 5Q)

⇒ 2Q2 (12 + 20 + 15)

⇒ 2 × 3² × (12 + 20 + 15)

⇒ 18 × 47 

⇒ 846 cm2
